issues.failure_explanation: Definition def:batchSampling only requires $\sum_i P_i\succ 0$; it permits a matrix $A$ with zero rows and a distribution that samples them. On a draw with all sampled rows zero, $S_\tau A_\tau=0$, so the proof applies Lemma lem2 outside its hypothesis (nonzero matrix, $\rank>0$) and divides by $\|S_\tau A_\tau\|_2^2=0$; the step is undefined on an event of possibly positive probability. Worse, for batch-size $q=1$ and a zero row $j$ with $p_{1j}>0$, the statement's own quantity $\beta^S_{1,j}=\max_{\tau_1=j}\|S_\tau A_\tau\|_2^2$ equals $0$, so $B_{S;1}$ is singular and $B_{S;1}^{-1/2}$ in (lem5Eq0), and hence $D$, $\eta$, $\xi$ of Theorem convRBSK and $B_S$ of Theorem convRBSK_relaxed_pave, do not exist, although the theorems claim these constants for every admissible sampling and every prescribed nonsingular diagonal $S$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standing hypothesis that every row index sampled with positive marginal probability indexes a nonzero row of $A$ (equivalently $\|S_\tau A_\tau\|_2>0$ almost surely), or adopt the convention that zero-block draws contribute $0$ (legitimate since then $r_\tau=0$); all statements and rates then stand unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma lem6 is unproven on a nonempty admissible part of its stated domain, and there the constants $B_{S;i}^{-1/2}$, $D$, $\eta$, $\xi$, $B_S$ of Theorem convRBSK, Corollary convRBSK_relaxed, Theorem convRBSK_relaxed_pave and Theorem convRBSK_sharper are undefined, so the advertised convergence-rate bounds are ill-posed in that regime.
issues.title: Lemma lem6's key step and constants break down for admissible samplings whose batches consist of zero rows
issues.why_classification: A single standard extra hypothesis (or a 0/0 convention) removes the degeneracy; the lemma's claim, the theorems' conclusions, rates and advertised scope all survive without any new argument.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lem4 gives $\E(XY)=\E[X\,\E(Y|X)]$ with $X=|s_{\tau_i}|^2|r_{\tau_i}|^2$, $Y=1/\|S_\tau A_\tau\|_2^2$. The next displayed equality asserts $\E(Y\mid |s_{\tau_i}|^2|r_{\tau_i}|^2)=\E(Y\mid\tau_i)$, which holds only if the map $j\mapsto |s_j|^2|r_j|^2$ is injective on the support of $\tau_i$; this is nowhere assumed. If two indices $j\neq j'$ share $|s_j|^2|r_j|^2$ but $\E(1/\|S_\tau A_\tau\|_2^2\mid\tau_i=j)\ne\E(\cdot\mid\tau_i=j')$, the two conditional expectations differ and the equality is false. The endpoint can only be reached by conditioning on $\tau_i$ directly, an inference the proof does not make.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Condition on $\tau_i$ directly: since $|s_{\tau_i}|^2|r_{\tau_i}|^2$ is $\sigma(\tau_i)$-measurable, $\E[XY]=\E[\,\E[XY\mid\tau_i]\,]=\sum_j p_{ij}|s_j|^2|r_j|^2\,\E(1/\|S_\tau A_\tau\|_2^2\mid\tau_i=j)$; a one-line rerouting, after which the lemma and all downstream uses are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the derivation of (lem5Eq2) inside Lemma lem6 contains a false inference, so the lemma and, through it, the estimates of Theorem convRBSK and its dependents lack valid support at this step.
issues.title: Lemma lem6's proof replaces conditioning on $|s_{\tau_i}|^2|r_{\tau_i}|^2$ by conditioning on $\tau_i$ without justification
issues.why_classification: The fix is a local rerouting of the same computation (condition on $\tau_i$ from the start); the lemma's statement and every guarantee built on it survive verbatim, so no substantive content is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: Inequality (thm4Eq5) is exactly Lemma lem5 applied to the paired sample sequences $\{\xi_{\tau^{(k-1,j)}}\}$ and $\{\|x^{(k,j)}-x_\star\|_2^2\}$, so the required hypothesis is that the sample covariance of $\xi$ with the SQUARED error norm is nonnegative. The theorem instead assumes $\cov(\xi_{\tau^{(k-1)}},\|x^{(k)}-x_\star\|_2)\ge0$, which does not imply it: for the $\ell=3$ paired samples $(\xi,\|x-x_\star\|_2)=((1,2),(0,1),(0,3))$ the sample covariance of $(\xi,\|x-x_\star\|_2)$ equals $0$ (hypothesis met), yet $(1/3)\sum_j\xi_j\|x_j-x_\star\|_2^2=4/3<14/9=(\frac13\sum\xi_j)(\frac13\sum\|x_j-x_\star\|_2^2)$, so (thm4Eq5) fails. The stated hypothesis therefore does not support the step that produces the contraction factor.

issues.overall_effect: Theorem convRBSK_sharper is not established under its stated hypothesis; the sample-mean-based factor $1+\epsilon-\E(\xi_\tau)$ in (thm4Eq2) (the bound plotted as 'Thm convRBSK_sharper bound' in the experiments) is unjustified as assumed.
issues.title: Theorem convRBSK_sharper assumes covariance with the error norm but its proof needs covariance with the squared norm
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local restatement of the assumed covariance to the quantity the proof actually uses; the theorem's form, conclusion and scope are preserved with no new argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which holds with probability at least $1-\delta$.

issues.failure_explanation: Inequality (thm4Eq8) holds only on the Hoeffding event of probability at least $1-\delta$; on the exceptional event the empirical factor $(1-\frac1\ell\sum_j\xi_j)$ can exceed $1+\epsilon-\E(\xi_{\tau^{(k-1)}})$ by an arbitrary amount, and the proof controls nothing there. 'Taking expectation on both sides' of an inequality valid only on that event is an invalid inference, so the deterministic population claim (thm4Eq2) is not derived. Moreover both sides of (thm4Eq2) are deterministic quantities, so the qualifier 'with probability at least $1-\delta$' attaches to no random experiment in the statement. What the argument supports is at most the empirical statement (thm4Eq8) with probability $1-\delta$, or a population bound under a population-level covariance condition; neither is the stated claim, and the assumed sample covariance over fresh independent copies does not control the covariance of the actual single process.

failure_location.quote: Taking expectation on both sides of (\ref{thm4Eq8}) leads to the sharper estimate (\ref{thm4Eq2}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either restate the conclusion as the empirical statement the proof yields — with probability at least $1-\delta$, $\frac1\ell\sum_j\E_k^{(j)}(\|x^{(k+1,j)}-x_\star\|_2^2)\le(1+\epsilon-\E(\xi_\tau))\,\frac1\ell\sum_j\|x^{(k,j)}-x_\star\|_2^2$ — or keep a population statement by assuming at population level $\cov(\xi_{\tau^{(k-1)}},\|x^{(k)}-x_\star\|_2^2)\ge 0$, in which case taking expectations in (thm1Eq3) directly gives $\E\|x^{(k+1)}-x_\star\|_2^2\le(1-\E(\xi_\tau))\,\E\|x^{(k)}-x_\star\|_2^2$ and the concentration inequality serves only to certify $\E(\xi_\tau)$ from samples. Both are contained repairs leaving a comparable per-step rate guarantee.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem convRBSK_sharper's stated guarantee — a with-probability-$1-\delta$ bound on the expected squared error with factor $1+\epsilon-\E(\xi_\tau)$ — is not established; the concentration-based 'sharper bound' tested throughout Section 5 is unsupported as stated.
issues.title: Theorem convRBSK_sharper's deterministic expectation bound is inferred from a only-with-probability-$1-\delta$ sample inequality
issues.why_classification: The repair requires restating what is random (or adding a population-level covariance hypothesis) rather than new proof architecture, and a recognizable comparable per-step bound survives; but the theorem's advertised expectation-type guarantee is not established as written, so the defect exceeds minor.
